I think water cooling can be quieter than fans, depending on the pump. But it's not much benefit unless you are overclocking.

Another question is what to do when the water evaporates from the water cooling?

It's usually a closed system. So any evaporated water re-condenses.
It's very much like a closed radiator system on a car. It uses coolant, not water.
Unless you are overclocking or really paranoid about burning out a $1000 cpu, I doubt it's worth the investment.
It works. Just like cooling with liquid nitrogen works. You just don't need it. Unless you do.

Like all cooling meathods I can think of, you'll eventually need to clean. With fans, you just need to remove dust from your blades/filters. With water cooling, you have to drain the loop, clean the damn thing, fill it back up and hope you don't dump coolant all over your components anywhere in there.
